open_findings.title: The shipped export builder has the data-disclosure half of F08 but not the access-control half
open_findings.finding: The allowlist, the free-text refusal and the compound-filename check are all in the shipped src/data/export.js, and the acceptance suite is green. But the retired src/output/recipients.js holds the permission table - makeDevIdentity, requireApprovedIdentity, canRead, canAttach - and the shipped module has no equivalent. That module is RETAINED deliberately for this reason; deleting it would delete the permission table.
open_findings.impact: F08's disclosure half is closed. Its access-control half is not: whether a participant may read a record, and refusal of a restricted attachment, are not enforced in what ships.
open_findings.handling: Wire the permission surface into the shipped builder, or state the restriction plainly as unimplemented. A browser-side allowlist is not access control, and no backend exists here to provide it.

open_findings.title: The candidate records carry no reporting period, and the source cannot supply one
open_findings.finding: ACCEPT-01 R27 fails and should stay failing. The 10543 candidate rows have no period, year or date field, though the screening rule is described as running on 2025/2024 and H1 2026/2025. Two rows also carry a null cost reconciliation because the price-file FOB value is empty - a null difference is not a match.
open_findings.handling: Needs a commercial or source input. Guessing the period is the one thing the brief forbids.

open_findings.title: The payload contains no comparable price observation that can be used
open_findings.finding: Every offer is excluded, dominated by PRODUCT_MATCH_UNRESOLVED (offers rest on seller cross-references, which is a candidate to inspect rather than approved equivalence) and PACK_CONTENTS_UNKNOWN (no offer declares whether its quote is for a piece or a pack). The panel is correct to exclude them all.
open_findings.impact: MARKET-07 has tested logic and a working screen but no answer. The commercial question - how our net terms compare with a competitor - cannot be answered from the data currently held.
open_findings.handling: Needs pack contents and an exact match basis in the source. No code change supplies either.

open_findings.title: The payload has no recorded digest, so an added key cannot be verified against the file's own statement
open_findings.finding: A key was added by hand to meta (marketComparisonDeclarations) because writing it back programmatically rewrote the envelope's recorded digest, which then no longer matched the file. The payload is excluded from version control, so it exists only on this machine with no history. The added key was verified against the authorised sibling copy instead: cases, candidateScreen, verifiedCosts, offers, sources and alternatives are all byte-identical, and exactly one key was added.
open_findings.impact: A restricted file that a reviewer cannot verify against its own recorded digest is weaker evidence than one that never carried the extra key. The byte difference is also explained: the repo copy is pretty-printed while the sibling is minified, which accounts for 1054709 of the 1054709 byte gap; the real content change is 2965 characters.
open_findings.handling: The right fix is a small builder in 01_data/91_build/ that regenerates the payload with its digest intact. That is outside the agent-owned area and is a decision about how the file should be produced.

open_findings.title: My own module_audit still over-reports, and the generated audits are stale
open_findings.finding: tools/module_audit.py is a raw text scan and cannot tell a deliberately declared comparison against a retired module from a misdirected load. It reports 11 retired loads where the guard says the genuinely misdirected count is 0. It now says so in its own output and names guard_09_module_scope.cjs as the authority. docs/ORPHAN_AUDIT.md and MODULE_AUDIT.md were also stale at commit time because the module lists changed after they were generated.
open_findings.handling: Either rework the tool to read the in-file declarations the way the guard does, or delete it and let the guard be the only answer. Regenerate both reports before any further commit.

open_findings.title: A country name appears where a distributor name is expected in the candidate rows
open_findings.finding: Candidate rows carry distributor labels ITUK and PORTUGAL. PORTUGAL is a country and the source never states which legal entity it is. ITUK and IUK are separate entities, and UTI and UMI must never be blended.
open_findings.handling: Not renamed - renaming would invent the entity. Kept visible with every label as it appears.

open_findings.title: One case's costRecordPresent flag contradicts verifiedCosts
open_findings.finding: IMOTORS-OIL (part 5876150530) carries a verified cost of 2.3995 EUR on the forward basis while its packEvidence.costRecordPresent is false. Checked all five cases: the flag agrees on four and disagrees on exactly this one. So the objectives tab can rank a gross-profit alternative while the economics tab says no cost is applied.
open_findings.handling: Both statements are individually defensible; together they would confuse a reader. Needs a decision on which is authoritative for this case.
